points.quote: Academic misconduct will occur where a student uses technological aids and/or Artificial Intelligence (AI) to gain an unfair advantage in meeting the assessment learning outcomes.
points.gist: Using technological aids or AI to gain an unfair advantage in meeting assessment learning outcomes counts as academic misconduct.

points.quote: Generating an assessment in its entirety and submitting it as the student’s own work.
points.gist: Generating a whole assessment with AI and submitting it as your own work is listed as unauthorised use.

points.quote: Failing to follow specific instructions relating to the use of AI within the assessment brief, except for documented inclusive support adjustments.
points.gist: Not following the assessment brief's AI instructions is misconduct, except for documented inclusive support adjustments.

points.quote: Acknowledge any use of GenAI in their work with appropriate referencing. Record how GenAI tools have been used by including screenshots of examples of the prompts used, and the output generated in your assignment coversheet.
points.gist: Students should reference any GenAI use and include screenshots of prompts and outputs in the assignment coversheet.

points.quote: Failing to acknowledge/reference any permitted use of AI within an assessment.
points.gist: Not acknowledging or referencing permitted AI use within an assessment is listed as misconduct.

points.quote: Attempting to use AI to humanise or attempt to hide the use of AI so that the submitted assessment does not reflect the student’s own understandings, thoughts or ideas.
points.gist: Using AI to humanise or hide AI use so work does not reflect the student's own understanding is misconduct.

points.quote: Uploading an assessment to be automatically rewritten or translated, so that the submitted assessment does not reflect the student’s own understandings, thoughts or ideas.
points.gist: Uploading an assessment to be automatically rewritten or translated, so it no longer reflects your own understanding, is misconduct.

points.quote: Failing to prevent built-in/preinstalled generative AI applications from producing substantial or significant portions of an assessment, which therefore do not reflect the student’s own understandings, thoughts or ideas.
points.gist: Failing to stop built-in or preinstalled generative AI from producing substantial parts of an assessment is misconduct.

points.quote: Unauthorised use of any other technological aid, such as translation software, paraphrasing tools, essay bots and generated of graphics or artwork, unless otherwise stated in the assessment brief.
points.gist: Other aids such as translation software, paraphrasing tools, essay bots and generated graphics are unauthorised unless the assessment brief says otherwise.

points.quote: If a student is in any doubt about what is considered acceptable usage of AI within a particular assessment, they should seek guidance from their module leader.
points.gist: Students in doubt about acceptable AI use in an assessment should ask their module leader.

points.quote: Keep drafts of work to evidence their thinking and the development of their submission.
points.gist: Students should keep drafts to evidence their thinking and how their submission developed.

points.quote: interpreting detection software reports, where the substance of the copied material will be considered as well as the quantity, and there is no percentage threshold for an investigation to be initiated
points.gist: Detection software reports are read for substance as well as quantity, and no percentage threshold triggers an investigation.

points.quote: A mark of 0% for the element of assessment which must be resubmitted where permitted*, to the required standard. The mark for the element of assessment following resubmission will be capped at the minimum pass mark.
points.gist: A Category 2 penalty is 0% for the element, resubmitted where permitted, with the resubmission mark capped at the minimum pass mark.

points.quote: Students can be excluded from the University for very serious or repeat offences.
points.gist: Students can be excluded from the University for very serious or repeat offences.

points.quote: The student may submit an appeal within 10 working days of the official notification of the outcome of a decision by the Academic Integrity Lead or the Academic Misconduct Committee in line with the Academic Appeals Procedure.
points.gist: Students may appeal within 10 working days of official notification of an Academic Integrity Lead or Committee decision.
